💡 Essential Arduino Projects — Code Templates

Non-Blocking LED Blink (millis() pattern)

const int LED = 13; unsigned long lastToggle = 0; const unsigned long INTERVAL = 500; bool ledState = false; void setup() { pinMode(LED, OUTPUT); } void loop() { if (millis() - lastToggle >= INTERVAL) { lastToggle = millis(); ledState = !ledState; digitalWrite(LED, ledState); } }

Ultrasonic Distance (HC-SR04)

const int TRIG = 9, ECHO = 10; void setup() { pinMode(TRIG, OUTPUT); pinMode(ECHO, INPUT); Serial.begin(9600); } void loop() { digitalWrite(TRIG, LOW); delayMicroseconds(2); digitalWrite(TRIG, HIGH); delayMicroseconds(10); digitalWrite(TRIG, LOW); long duration = pulseIn(ECHO, HIGH); float distance = duration * 0.034 / 2; Serial.print("Distance: "); Serial.print(distance); Serial.println(" cm"); delay(100); }

External Interrupt Button

volatile int count = 0; void buttonISR() { count++; } void setup() { Serial.begin(9600); pinMode(2, INPUT_PULLUP); attachInterrupt(digitalPinToInterrupt(2), buttonISR, FALLING); } void loop() { Serial.println(count); delay(500); }

🏭 FPGA Internal Architecture

LUT (Look-Up Table)

The fundamental building block. An N-input LUT can implement ANY Boolean function of N inputs. Typically 4–6 input LUTs.

4-input LUT: 16-bit SRAM stores truth table. Inputs select which SRAM bit to output.

Flip-Flop (FF)

D flip-flop following each LUT. Registers intermediate results, enables pipelining and synchronous design.

One LUT + one FF = one "slice" or "LE" (Logic Element)

Block RAM (BRAM)

Dedicated SRAM blocks — typically 18Kb or 36Kb each. Used for FIFOs, frame buffers, lookup tables.

Dual-port — read and write simultaneously at different addresses.

DSP Blocks

Hardened multiplier-accumulator blocks. Much faster and smaller than building a multiplier from LUTs.

Xilinx DSP48E2: 27×18 MAC, pre-adder, cascade — for FIR filters, FFT, matrix multiply.

⚡ Linux Interrupt Handling

Two-Stage Interrupt Handling

Top Half (hardirq)

  • Runs immediately when hardware interrupt fires
  • Runs with interrupts disabled (non-preemptible)
  • Must be extremely fast
  • Cannot sleep, cannot block
  • Saves data for bottom half

Bottom Half (deferred work)

The actual processing is deferred to lower-priority context. Three mechanisms:

  • Softirq: Runs in interrupt context, no sleep. Network RX/TX, SCSI
  • Tasklet: Built on softirq — easier to use
  • Workqueue: Runs in kernel thread — CAN sleep. Most flexible

Threaded Interrupt Handlers (PREEMPT_RT)

With the PREEMPT_RT patch, device drivers can register threaded IRQ handlers:

request_threaded_irq(irq, quick_handler, // Top half - hardirq context thread_handler, // Bottom half - RT kernel thread IRQF_TRIGGER_FALLING, "my_device", dev);

The thread_handler runs in a SCHED_FIFO kernel thread — schedulable, can set priority, can sleep. This is how RT Linux achieves predictable latency.

🧵 Kernel Threads

Kernel threads run entirely in kernel space — no user-space memory map. Created with kthread_create() or kthread_run():

struct task_struct *task = kthread_run(my_thread_fn, data, "my_thread"); int my_thread_fn(void *data) { while (!kthread_should_stop()) { // periodic work msleep(100); } return 0; }

Kernel Thread Use Cases

  • ksoftirqd — processes softirq backlog
  • kworker — workqueue processing
  • IRQ threads (threaded interrupts)
  • Driver polling threads
  • Real-time data processing pipeline

📊 Case Study 1: Data Acquisition System (DAS)

A multi-channel DAS for industrial monitoring collects analog sensor data, digitizes it, processes it, stores it locally, and transmits to a SCADA server.

LayerComponentSpecification
SensorsTemperature (PT100), Pressure (4–20mA), Vibration (MEMS accelerometer)8 analog channels
Signal Conditioning4–20mA receiver, RTD excitation + INA, anti-aliasing filter0–3.3V output to ADC
ADCADS8688 — 16-bit, 8-channel, SPI500 ksps aggregate
ProcessorSTM32H743 — ARM Cortex-M7 @ 480 MHzDMA-driven ADC sampling
Storage8GB eMMC — circular bufferFAT32, stores 30 days of data
CommunicationEthernet (MODBUS TCP) + LoRaWAN for remote sites100 Mbps Ethernet, 2 km LoRa range
Display4.3" touch LCD — real-time trend graphs800×480 TFT, LVGL library
Power24V DC + UPS battery backup + isolated DC-DCContinuous operation, surge protection

Software Architecture (RTOS-based)

  • ADC_Sampler (Priority 5): DMA interrupt fills ping-pong buffer, triggers Processing via semaphore
  • Signal_Processor (Priority 4): Calibration, unit conversion, statistical analysis (RMS, peak, average)
  • Storage_Writer (Priority 3): Writes time-stamped records to eMMC in batch
  • Network_Comm (Priority 3): MODBUS TCP server, responds to SCADA polls
  • Display_Update (Priority 1): Updates trend graphs every 100ms
🏭 Case Study 2: Industrial PLC-Based Motor Control

Hardware Components

  • Controller: PLC (Siemens S7-1200) + ARM Cortex-M4 custom motion control board
  • Drive: Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) — 3-phase AC motor speed control via PWM
  • Feedback: 2500 PPR incremental encoder for position/speed, current sensors (LEM HAIS) for torque estimation
  • Safety: Hardware E-stop circuit (hard-wired, not software), safety relay, thermal overload relay
  • HMI: SCADA touch panel — speed setpoint, real-time graphs, alarm management

Control Loop (1ms hard real-time)

Encoder → Speed Calculator → PID Controller → PWM setpoint → VFD → Motor → Encoder (closed loop). The inner control loop runs every 1ms (1 kHz) in a high-priority RTOS task. The outer position loop runs at 10ms.

🎧 Case Study 3: Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) Headphones

How ANC Works

  • Feedforward mic: Microphone outside the ear cup captures ambient noise
  • DSP processing: DSP predicts noise at the ear, generates anti-noise signal (180° phase-inverted)
  • Speaker output: Anti-noise played through speaker — destructive interference cancels ambient noise
  • Feedback mic: Inside earcup — monitors residual noise, provides error signal for adaptive filter
  • LMS adaptive algorithm: Continuously updates filter coefficients to minimize residual noise

Hardware Requirements

  • DSP core: ARM Cortex-M33 with DSP extensions (or dedicated BT+ANC chip)
  • ADC: 24-bit sigma-delta for microphone, >100 ksps
  • Processing latency: <100µs from mic to speaker
  • Power: <30mW for ANC circuit — battery life critical

Processing Pipeline

Trigger (external light barrier) → Capture frame → ISP processing → DMA to DDR → NPU inference (<10ms) → Decision logic → GPIO output (accept/reject) → Log + stream to server. Total latency target: <50ms.

🔤 Multiple Choice Questions — Fundamentals to Tools
  1. Which dependability attribute measures the fraction of time a system is operational?
    a) Reliability   b) Safety   c) Availability   d) Maintainability
    Answer: c — Availability = MTBF / (MTBF + MTTR)
  2. An embedded system that MUST respond within a strict deadline where missing it causes catastrophic failure is:
    a) Soft Real-Time   b) Firm Real-Time   c) Hard Real-Time   d) Non-Real-Time
    Answer: c — Airbag, pacemaker, flight control = Hard RT.
  3. The Intel 4004 (1971) is historically significant because it was:
    a) First computer   b) First transistor   c) First commercial microprocessor   d) First RISC processor
    Answer: c
  4. In cross-compilation, the HOST is:
    a) The target MCU   b) The development PC running the compiler   c) The JTAG debugger   d) The oscilloscope
    Answer: b
  5. Which tool verifies all program symbols are resolved and assigns memory addresses?
    a) Compiler   b) Assembler   c) Simulator   d) Linker
    Answer: d
  6. The Waterfall model's biggest disadvantage is:
    a) Too fast   b) Too cheap   c) Difficult to accommodate late requirement changes   d) No documentation
    Answer: c
🔤 MCQ — RTOS, DSP, ADC/DAC
  1. In FreeRTOS, which primitive protects a shared SPI bus (mutual exclusion)?
    a) Binary Semaphore   b) Mutex   c) Event Group   d) Queue
    Answer: b — Mutex has priority inheritance to prevent priority inversion.
  2. What is the key advantage of a microkernel over a monolithic kernel?
    a) Faster system calls   b) Simpler design   c) Higher reliability — kernel crash doesn't crash whole OS   d) Lower memory usage
    Answer: c
  3. Saturation arithmetic in DSP prevents:
    a) Division by zero   b) Overflow wrapping that causes signal distortion   c) Memory leaks   d) Pipeline hazards
    Answer: b
  4. A 10-bit ADC with Vref = 5V has an LSB voltage of:
    a) 5 mV   b) 10 mV   c) 4.88 mV   d) 1.22 mV
    Answer: c — LSB = 5V/1024 = 4.88 mV
  5. Which ADC type achieves the highest resolution (24-bit) at the cost of slow speed?
    a) Flash ADC   b) SAR ADC   c) Pipeline ADC   d) Sigma-Delta ADC
    Answer: d
  6. The 4-20mA current loop uses 4mA as "live zero" to:
    a) Reduce power   b) Distinguish dead wire (0mA) from minimum signal (4mA)   c) Increase accuracy   d) Match ADC range
    Answer: b

💼 Interview Questions — Senior Embedded Engineer Level
  1. Q: Explain priority inversion and how RTOS mutexes solve it.
    A: Priority inversion occurs when a high-priority task waits for a resource held by a low-priority task that gets preempted by a medium-priority task. Solution: Priority Inheritance — the mutex-holding low-priority task temporarily inherits the waiting high-priority task's priority. Famous example: Mars Pathfinder 1997 reset loops.
  2. Q: Difference between a semaphore and a mutex — when to use each?
    A: Mutex: ownership, priority inheritance, for mutual exclusion. Binary Semaphore: no ownership, for signaling (ISR → task). Use mutex to protect shared resources; semaphore for task synchronization.
  3. Q: How does Sigma-Delta ADC achieve 24-bit resolution from a 1-bit internal modulator?
    A: Oversampling at very high rates + noise shaping pushes quantization noise to high frequencies. The digital decimation filter then low-pass filters and downsamples, extracting fine amplitude resolution. Every 4× oversampling adds roughly 1 ENOB.
  4. Q: Describe Linux interrupt handling flow from hardware IRQ to userspace.
    A: Hardware IRQ fires → kernel hardirq handler (top half) acknowledges, saves minimal data, flags bottom half → softirq/tasklet/workqueue runs the actual processing → data placed in kernel buffer → blocked user process woken via wake_up_interruptible() → process reads via copy_to_user().
  5. Q: A sensor produces 0–100mV differential signal with 5V common-mode noise on a 10m cable. How would you interface it to a 12-bit ADC?
    A: Use a 4–20mA transmitter to eliminate common-mode/cable issues, OR use differential twisted-pair + shield with an Instrumentation Amplifier (INA128) — 90dB+ CMRR rejects the 5V common-mode. Amplify 0-100mV to 0-3.3V (gain≈33), add anti-aliasing filter, and isolation if grounds float.
